label: tbl:notation-register-table3-data
title: Data table 3 from
html:
Concept Font Symbols
Crossing energy plain italic E_{\mathfrak{H}} — total crossing energy of hadron \mathfrak{H}. E_{\mathfrak{H}} = \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{H}} \cdot c_q^2.
Hecke amplitude plain italic + roman subscript h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1} — the Hecke-relation trace \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_i) (\sigma_i^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}}\sigma_i + \mathbf{1}; equivalently the Skein amplitude \sigma_i - \sigma_i^{-1} = h_{\mathrm{A}}). Not the discriminant: for \sigma_i^2 - h_{\mathrm{A}}\sigma_i - \mathbf{1} = 0 the discriminant is h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 + 4 = [2]_q^2, so \sqrt{\mathrm{disc}} = [2]_q is the other crossing weight — the bar-even one, against h_{\mathrm{A}} bar-odd, the scalar shift carried by typed crossings (\mathfrak{d}-type -h_{\mathrm{A}}, mixed -h_{\mathrm{A}}/2); \approx 0.209 at q_0. Older text splits this between "\mathrm{HA}" (acronym) and a bare "H_A"; the bare form collided with the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_A(q) on A strands (H-family symbols always carry an argument). Compute-layer witness keys (derived_50_digit.H_A, parameters.HA) keep their older names.
Hook-length product Latin cap + arg H_q(\lambda) = \prod_{x \in \lambda} [h_x(\lambda)]_q — always with partition argument.
Iwahori–Hecke algebra Latin cap H_n(q) — always with subscript n.
Atomic braid word calligraphic \mathcal{B}_K \in H_{3A}(q) — canonical atomic braid for atom K = (Z, N) with A = Z + N. Factorises as \mathcal{B}_K = \mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}} \cdot \bowtie_K (vacuum · interface). Relocated from \beta_K to cal — the cal register was expanded to admit Hecke-algebra structural elements alongside bundles/sheaves.
Vacuum (constit) factor calligraphic + superscript \mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}} = \mathcal{B}_p^{(1)} \cdots \mathcal{B}_p^{(Z)} \mathcal{B}_n^{(1)} \cdots \mathcal{B}_n^{(N)} — disjoint Hecke product of per-nucleon 3-strand blocks (no interface generators), i.e. "constituent vacuum". Synonym for the older \beta_K^{\mathrm{constit}}.
Proton / neutron H_3 braid calligraphic \mathcal{B}_p, \mathcal{B}_n \in H_3(q) — canonical 3-strand intra-nucleon braids (quark content u-u-d / u-d-d). Relocated from \beta_p, \beta_n.
Intra-atom interface operator bowtie + K subscript \bowtie_K — K-deformed Hopf-link-style operator at strand-block boundaries of atom K; \mathcal{B}_K = \mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}} \cdot \bowtie_K. Always adorned with K subscript (no bare \bowtie for this concept). Replacement for \Delta_I^K.
Inter-block Hopf-link operation \oplus X \oplus Y — Hopf-link / fusion of two composite structures (e.g., Z\mathfrak{p} \oplus N\mathfrak{n} = Z proton blocks Hopf-linked with N neutron blocks). Relocated from bare \bowtie to disambiguate from intra-atom \bowtie_K.
Hopf link object calligraphic \mathcal{L}_K, \mathcal{L}_H — the Hopf link as a knot/link object. \mathcal{L}_H is the standard Hopf link in the appendix mass-formula notation; \mathcal{L}_K is the K-parameterized variant.
Frobenius Gram matrix upright cap + arg \mathrm{G}(q) \in \mathrm{Mat}_N(R) — Gram matrix of the chosen N-element Frobenius basis at Hecke parameter q, with R the Hecke base ring (not \mathbb{R}). Currently a matrix-valued function \mathrm{G}: \mathbb{R} \to \mathrm{Mat}_N(R), q \mapsto \mathrm{G}(q); whether it promotes to a functor (with a Reeb source category) is not settled here, since Reeb is not formalized as a category. Upright distinguishes from gravitational scalar G_q (italic, q-subscript).
Markov trace upright lc + M \mathrm{tr}_M — Jones–Markov trace on H_n(q); \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K) = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda(\mathcal{B}_K). Lowercase upright matches the universal \mathrm{tr} convention (parallel to \det, \dim, \mathrm{Hom}). Distinct from fibre functor \tau (italic Greek).
Jones–Markov central coefficient plain italic y_\lambda — coefficient in \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda, given by Wenzl's hook–content closed form [wenzl1988]. Non-negative under the production convention D: y_{(n-k,k)} = [n-2k+1]_q/[2]_q^n on the two-row stratum, and y_\lambda = 0 identically for \ell(\lambda) \geq 3. Older text records "sign-indefinite at n \geq 4" — that was the excised convention C, whose first negative entry was y_{(1^4)} = -0.00084253 at q_0; withdrawn 2026-08-09. Distinct from the Plancherel measure w_\lambda and the q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight w_\lambda(q) at q \neq 1 — coincides with w_\lambda only on the self-conjugate stratum (see prop:wedderburn-weight-canonical). Never confuse with u_\lambda (LP shadow-price).
LP shadow-price plain italic u_\lambda, u_0 — Schrijver linear-programming convention for operator-selection LP dual variables. Non-negative by LP duality. Never write y_\lambda here.
Markov parameter plain italic z = q^3/(q^2+1) = q^2/[2]_q — the Markov-trace loop value \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) of the stabilisation axiom; convention D of the trace-convention registry and the framework's production trace, z(q_0) = 0.61268803714646525160. Older text writes z = 1/(\check q + \check q^{-1}) = 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) — convention C, excised by the owner ruling of 2026-08-09. C is not a variant normalisation of the same quantity, and the \check q spelling is what made the substitution look harmless. Under this paper's Hecke normalisation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + \mathbf{1} the Temperley–Lieb generator is e_i := q - \sigma_i, which satisfies e_i^2 = [2]_q\,e_i; the loop parameter is therefore \delta = [2]_q = q + q^{-1}, not q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}. Convention D reproduces the Jones–Temperley–Lieb normalisation exactly — \mathrm{tr}_M(e_i) = q - z = q/(q^2+1) = 1/[2]_q = 1/\delta, the sorry-free loop_reciprocal of TemperleyLiebTower.lean — whereas C assigned a loop reciprocal to the Hecke generator \sigma_i, and at x = q^{1/2} rather than x = q in 1/(x + x^{-1}): 1/\delta = 0.4972905456 against z_C = 0.4993203342, one square root and 0.408\,\% apart. Never write 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) for 1/\delta (bean qou-98g5). Under D the three-strand weights are (y_{(3)}, y_{(2,1)}, y_{(1^3)}) = ([4]_q/[2]_q^3,\ 1/[2]_q^2,\ 0) = (0.5054042,\ 0.2472979,\ 0); under C they were (0.4153958,\ 0.2809296,\ 0.0227449). The selection is forced, not stipulated — see rem:markov-axioms-primitive.
Mass (knot) fraktur \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{K}} — knot mass.
Plancherel measure (classical) plain italic w_\lambda(1) := (\dim V_\lambda)^2 / n! — the classical Plancherel probability measure on partitions \lambda \vdash n, with \dim V_\lambda the q-independent (classical) Hecke-irrep dimension (= number of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda). Sums to 1 exactly in \mathbb{Q}. See prop:plancherel-weight-boundedness. Distinct from the q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight w_\lambda(q); the two coincide at q = 1 only.
Quantum dimension plain italic \dim_q(\lambda) = [n]_q! / \prod_{x \in \lambda} [h_x]_q — the q-deformed Frame–Robinson–Thrall hook-length dimension. Reduces to \dim V_\lambda at q = 1. Used in the q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight w_\lambda(q) = \dim_q^2(\lambda)/[n]_q!.
Spinor information rate plain italic with háček \check{q} — eigenvalue of the elementary half-twist on the spin-½ fundamental rep of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), \check{q}^2 = q. The "rate per half-twist" along a single linear braid (no surface area). Analogous to i: -1 as \check{q}: q — the algebraic ingredient that lifts the 1-D adjoint braid algebra to the 2-D spinor (spin-½) representation. The háček (Czech, "little hook") encodes the relation \check{q}^2 = q in the glyph. Older text writes r for this, and the Habiro literature writes u = q^{1/2}; r is reserved here for radius / generic-real contexts. Never use r, t (clashes with V_K(t) knot variable), \iota (clashes with involution / inclusion), or bare u for q^{1/2}.
Wedderburn-block weight (q-deformed) plain italic with tilde w_\lambda(q) := \dim_q^2(\lambda) / [n]_q! — the q-deformed analogue of the classical Plancherel measure w_\lambda. Not a probability measure at q \neq 1: empirically \sum_\lambda w_\lambda(q) \approx 1.51 at q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps) for n = 12. Specialises to w_\lambda at q = 1. Used in prop:plancherel-term-7-formulation and the q-deformed Wedderburn-block normalisation of prop:wedderburn-weight-canonical. Never call this "Plancherel weight" without the tilde — the classical Plancherel w_\lambda is a different, smaller object.
Wenzl principal-spec length Greek \ell — number of points in the Schur principal specialisation s_\lambda(1, q^2, q^4, \ldots, q^{2(\ell-1)}) defining y_\lambda via Wenzl's formula. Older text writes r_W for this, from a period when the spinor rate was written r; the spinor rate is now \check{q}.
Substrate phase angle plain italic \theta + q-subscript \theta_q — the phase (argument) of the complex substrate parameter, q = \lvert q\rvert e^{i\theta_q}; the \mathrm{U}(1) / Reeb rotation coordinate \rho_{\theta_q}. Distinct from the contact form \varTheta (upper-case) and from bare \theta (generic angle). Introduced to replace an earlier \varTheta overload in the complex-substrate material of §6.
Root-of-unity order plain italic r — the order of the primitive root of unity q = e^{i\pi/r} at which [r]_q vanishes and the representation category truncates (Verlinde / Reshetikhin–Turaev level); cyclotomic field \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_r). Standard quantum-topology name. An integer (r \in \mathbb{N}), disambiguated from the generic-real / radius r by its role as a subscript on \zeta and argument of [\,\cdot\,]_q. Older text writes \kappa for this; \kappa is retained here for the chart-transition gluing scalar z\,w = \kappa = q^{-1}.
Braid / Hecke generator indexing subscripted \sigma Braid-group B_n and Hecke H_n(q) generators are 0-indexed: \sigma_0, \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{n-2}, matching the compute layer. This is the convention throughout §6 and the particle-interactions chapter. The braid relation is \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} and far-commutation \sigma_i \sigma_j = \sigma_j \sigma_i for \lvert i - j\rvert \ge 2. Exception. prop:ew-slot-far-commutation-obstruction (and its coupled thm:hoefsmit-ew-cell-content) keeps 1-indexed generators \sigma_1, \sigma_3, \sigma_5 (slots) / \sigma_2, \sigma_4 (inter-slot), because those indices are semantically tied to the physical strand-pairs 1–2, 3–4, 5–6 (the natural \sigma_i \leftrightarrow strands i, i{+}1 reading) and are baked into the Lean obstruction proof; re-indexing would desynchronize the two statements without changing the mathematics.
